question: Should ambiguous outbound rows with no reconciliation-capable adapter remain pending indefinitely with backoff and unchanged retry budget, rather than eventually dead-lettering under the normal retry cap?
rationale: Both choices are technically defensible but intentionally trade permanent message loss against persistent pending state, audit timing, queue growth, and operator cleanup; tests cannot determine the product policy.

options.title: Keep rows recoverable
options.body: Approve the PR policy, retain unreconcilable ambiguous rows pending with backoff, and track operator visibility and cleanup with the broader delivery-ledger work.

options.title: Require bounded retention
options.body: Define an age- or policy-based terminal transition and operator-resolution path before merging so ambiguous rows cannot remain pending indefinitely.

options.title: Retain current terminal policy
options.body: Pause or close this mitigation until relevant adapters can reconcile unknown sends, accepting that capped rows may become permanently unrecoverable.

recommendation.title: Keep rows recoverable
recommendation.body: Approve the PR policy, retain unreconcilable ambiguous rows pending with backoff, and track operator visibility and cleanup with the broader delivery-ledger work.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved question is a core message-delivery and persistent-state policy decision rather than a mechanical code repair.
